status.pending_cert: DNS is in place. The certificate is being issued.

dns.txt: 1. Proof that the domain is yours
dns.txtHelp: A TXT record. Keep it as long as the domain is used here.
dns.aHelp: An A record pointing at our server address.
dns.cnameHelp: A CNAME record. Some providers call this an alias.
dns.note: Depending on your provider, DNS changes take a few minutes to a few hours to reach everyone.
dns.ttl: Tip before you switch: set the TTL of your records to 5 minutes (300 seconds) first, then the change takes effect quickly. You can raise it again afterwards.

registrars.title: Where do I find the DNS settings?
registrars.description: Add the records above wherever your domain is registered. Here are the paths for the most common providers.

ionos.label: IONOS
ionos.path: Menu Domains and SSL → click the domain → DNS tab → Add record.
ionos.note: For the A record leave the hostname field empty or enter {'@'}; for the CNAME enter www.

strato.label: Strato
strato.path: Customer area → Domains → Domain management → gear icon next to the domain → DNS settings.
strato.note: Strato allows CNAME only for subdomains such as www. The main domain therefore needs the A record above.

united.label: United Domains
united.path: Domain portfolio → click the domain → DNS → Manage DNS records.
united.note: There the A record uses name {'@'} and the CNAME uses name www. Changes only apply once you save.

hetzner.label: Hetzner
hetzner.path: DNS Console at dns.hetzner.com → select the zone → Add record.
hetzner.note: This only applies if the nameservers of your domain point at Hetzner. If another provider is listed there, the records belong there instead.

cloudflare.label: Cloudflare
cloudflare.path: Dashboard → click the domain → DNS → Records → Add record.
cloudflare.note: Important: set the proxy status to DNS only (grey cloud). With the orange cloud your domain points at Cloudflare instead of at us, and our check fails.

other.label: Other provider
other.path: Look for DNS, zone editor or nameserver records in the customer area of your provider.
other.note: If there is no DNS section, another service manages your nameservers — the records belong there. The three records themselves are the same everywhere.
